results.finding: Fixed in the doc and kit on 2026-11-14; this case keeps the old instructions as a regression check. src/06-java.md:30, :44 (and template.yaml at :962) say JDK 8 + kit (agent + -Djdk.tls.client.protocols=TLSv1.3,TLSv1.2) gives PQ. Observed on Corretto 8u512 (Lambda java8.al2, lambda/java:8.al2023 image, amazoncorretto:8 on ECS): with HttpsURLConnection every handshake fails, PQ and classical, with BCJSSE 'certificate_unknown(46) <- No hostname specified for HTTPS endpoint ID check'. JDK 8's HttpsURLConnection creates the socket without a host name; BCJSSE 1.78+ fails endpoint identification by default then (bc-java issue #1656). Adding -Dorg.bouncycastle.jsse.client.assumeOriginalHostName=true to JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS fixes it (PQ on all targets, case java-lambda-j8-bundled-hostfix). The tab's JDK 8 test used raw SSLSocket, not HttpsURLConnection. JDK 11+ is not affected.

results.finding: Fixed in the doc and kit on 2026-11-14; this case keeps the old instructions as a regression check. src/06-java.md:30, :44 (and template.yaml at :962) say JDK 8 + kit (agent + -Djdk.tls.client.protocols=TLSv1.3,TLSv1.2) gives PQ. Observed on Corretto 8u512 (Lambda java8.al2, lambda/java:8.al2023 image, amazoncorretto:8 on ECS): with HttpsURLConnection every handshake fails, PQ and classical, with BCJSSE 'certificate_unknown(46) <- No hostname specified for HTTPS endpoint ID check'. JDK 8's HttpsURLConnection creates the socket without a host name; BCJSSE 1.78+ fails endpoint identification by default then (bc-java issue #1656). Adding -Dorg.bouncycastle.jsse.client.assumeOriginalHostName=true to JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS fixes it (PQ on all targets, case java-lambda-j8-bundled-hostfix). The tab's JDK 8 test used raw SSLSocket, not HttpsURLConnection. JDK 11+ is not affected.

BCJSSE honours the same property, so on Lambda the flag is required with the kit; in containers and EC2 with 8u512 it is not (java-fargate-corretto8-agent-noproto is PQ without it). The flag in JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS overrides Lambda's value.

results.finding: Fixed in the doc and kit on 2026-11-14; this case keeps the old instructions as a regression check. src/06-java.md:30, :44 (and template.yaml at :962) say JDK 8 + kit (agent + -Djdk.tls.client.protocols=TLSv1.3,TLSv1.2) gives PQ. Observed on Corretto 8u512 (Lambda java8.al2, lambda/java:8.al2023 image, amazoncorretto:8 on ECS): with HttpsURLConnection every handshake fails, PQ and classical, with BCJSSE 'certificate_unknown(46) <- No hostname specified for HTTPS endpoint ID check'. JDK 8's HttpsURLConnection creates the socket without a host name; BCJSSE 1.78+ fails endpoint identification by default then (bc-java issue #1656). Adding -Dorg.bouncycastle.jsse.client.assumeOriginalHostName=true to JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS fixes it (PQ on all targets, case java-lambda-j8-bundled-hostfix). The tab's JDK 8 test used raw SSLSocket, not HttpsURLConnection. JDK 11+ is not affected.

results.finding: Fixed in the doc and kit on 2026-11-14; this case keeps the old instructions as a regression check. src/06-java.md:30 ('SunJSSE, TLS 1.2 client default'), :376 ('8 defaults clients to TLS 1.2') and :445 state it for JDK 8 generally. Observed: only the Lambda Java 8 runtime sets jdk.tls.client.protocols=TLSv1.2,TLSv1.1,TLSv1 (java8.al2 zip and the lambda/java:8.al2023 image, also under the image's own RIE without LocalStack); a plain Corretto 8u512 (amazoncorretto:8, and /var/lang/bin/java in the Lambda image started directly) offers TLS 1.3 by default (classical P-256 here). BCJSSE honours the same property, so on Lambda the flag is required with the kit; in containers and EC2 with 8u512 it is not (java-fargate-corretto8-agent-noproto is PQ without it). The flag in JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS overrides Lambda's value.

Observed on Corretto 8u512 (Lambda java8.al2, lambda/java:8.al2023 image, amazoncorretto:8 on ECS): with HttpsURLConnection every handshake fails, PQ and classical, with BCJSSE 'certificate_unknown(46) <- No hostname specified for HTTPS endpoint ID check'. JDK 8's HttpsURLConnection creates the socket without a host name; BCJSSE 1.78+ fails endpoint identification by default then (bc-java issue #1656). Adding -Dorg.bouncycastle.jsse.client.assumeOriginalHostName=true to JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS fixes it (PQ on all targets, case java-lambda-j8-bundled-hostfix). The tab's JDK 8 test used raw SSLSocket, not HttpsURLConnection. JDK 11+ is not affected.

results.finding: Fixed in the doc on 2026-11-14; kept as a regression check. AL2023 dnf nodejs20 (20.20.2) links the system OpenSSL 3.5.8, so it negotiates X25519MLKEM768 once the crypto policy is DEFAULT:PQ or OPENSSL_CONF points at openssl-pq-node-system.cnf, exactly like nodejs22/24. The tab says the opposite: src/05-nodejs.md l.25 ('20.x ... No / No / No ... Upgrade; no setting adds PQ'), l.38 ('any Node below 22.20 / 24.5: upgrade ... There is no setting') and l.5 ('anything on Node 20 or older'). l.452 already notes this for Debian 13's Node 20; the l.26 AL2023 row should cover nodejs20 too, and the rule should be 'check process.versions.openssl'.

results.finding: Fixed in the doc on 2026-11-14; kept as a regression check. AL2023 dnf nodejs20 (20.20.2) links the system OpenSSL 3.5.8, so it negotiates X25519MLKEM768 once the crypto policy is DEFAULT:PQ or OPENSSL_CONF points at openssl-pq-node-system.cnf, exactly like nodejs22/24. The tab says the opposite: src/05-nodejs.md l.25 ('20.x ... No / No / No ... Upgrade; no setting adds PQ'), l.38 ('any Node below 22.20 / 24.5: upgrade ... There is no setting') and l.5 ('anything on Node 20 or older'). l.452 already notes this for Debian 13's Node 20; the l.26 AL2023 row should cover nodejs20 too, and the rule should be 'check process.versions.openssl'.
